taxonomy.client_type_notes: Jefferson Lab is a DOE-owned FFRDC operated by Jefferson Science Associates (a contractor consortium). The contracting party from BFA's perspective is JSA, LLC, but ultimate ownership is federal civilian (DOE Office of Science). This is a multi-tenancy and vocabulary tension — see retro.
taxonomy.program_type_notes: Building 87 was originally a pre-engineered structure renovated into an office building per the A-001 narrative; it sits within a federal science research campus (Jefferson Lab is a particle physics accelerator facility). Best-fit top-level program is science_research because the project context is the campus mission, but the specific building's function reads more as commercial_office. Encoded as science_research because project context dominates; flagged for retro.
taxonomy.construction_scope_notes: Lightning protection scope doesn't map cleanly to construction_scope vocabulary; closest TWT-original entry is electronic_safety_security (which the vocab definition says includes 'fire alarm, access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection' — lightning protection isn't explicitly listed). taxonomy.bfa_role_notes: Architecture sealed by Dills Architects (Clay C. Dills, AIA, VA Lic. 013034). BFA's contribution is the electrical drawings ED-101 (lightning protection demolition) and E-101 (lightning protection new work), sealed by Richard H. Williams, PE (VA Lic. 048025). However, the PO is issued directly to BFA ('Order To: BOWMAN FOSTER AND ASSOCIATES INC'), which suggests BFA may be the prime A-E with Dills as architecture sub. This is an ambiguity worth flagging.

sheets.title: COVER SHEET
sheets.reading_notes: Standard JLab cover sheet. Shows Jefferson Lab campus location map ('WORK LOCATION' arrow points to Building 87 in northern portion of campus) and regional vicinity map (Newport News / Fort Eustis / Langley AFB / Poquoson / Hampton). Sealed by Richard H. Williams PE (BFA) — interesting that the COVER is sealed by BFA's PE rather than the architect; consistent with BFA being the prime A-E. Index of drawings lists 7 sheets total. Designer: RHW; Drawn: LAW. JLab title block lists ES&H Manager S. Hoey, Fire Protection Manager T. Minga, Design Manager S. Chandra, Engineering Manager J. Dolbeck, FM&L Division Manager J. Sprouse.

sheets.title: LEGENDS, ABBREVIATIONS AND NOTES
sheets.reading_notes: Architectural legend, abbreviations, materials legend (cover board, batt insulation, plywood, wood blocking, rigid insulation), 10 general notes, and a 4-paragraph PROJECT NARRATIVE that supplements the task order. Narrative confirms 6,720 SF building, 1996 construction, original building 'later renovated into an office building' (this clarifies current building use vs. task order which doesn't state current function). Specifies new roof system: 'mechanically adhered EPDM roof over 1 1/2" polyisocyanurate insulation.' Notes scope to 'temporarily remove and then reinstall' rooftop lightning protection grid; 'existing vertical down conductors and the rest of the protection system shall remain.' Notes non-working antenna on north side to be removed and exhaust fans + circuits to be demolished back to panelboard. Sealed by Clay C. Dills, AIA (Dills Architects). Designer: MKH; Drawn: TBB; both 8/16/2022.

sheets.title: DEMOLITION ROOF PLAN
sheets.reading_notes: 1/8"=1'-0" demo plan with one 1 1/2"=1'-0" enlarged demo/new-work detail. Building footprint 107'-5" ± x 62'-3" ± (~6,687 SF — corroborates 6,720 stated SF). Four photographic elevations: existing lighting rod, existing typical solatube, existing antenna, existing mech vent. 10 demolition key notes covering gutters, solatubes (remove and store), VTRs (must remain), mech roof vents, lightning protection grid (remove and store), splash blocks, coping, antenna (per ED101), and metal roof edge flashing. Owner-occupied during construction per general note 1. Architect-sealed.

sheets.title: ROOF PLAN
sheets.reading_notes: New-work 1/8"=1'-0" roof plan with same 107'-5" x 62'-3" footprint. Detail callouts to A-501 (A1 roof edge, B1 roof edge/parapet, A3 solatube curb, D1 vent thru roof). 11 key work notes: pre-finished metal gutters/downspouts, 12" prefab solatube curbs, VTR retention, deck patching, lightning protection reinstallation reference, splash block replacement, prefinished metal coping, walkway pads, ladder tie-off, commercial safety ladder dock, fall restraint anchors (Honeywell Miller Fusion roof anchor post). Approximately 13-14 solatubes shown distributed across roof plus 2 mech vent locations near center. Slope arrows show roof crown along centerline draining north and south to gutters. Architect-sealed.

sheets.title: DETAILS
sheets.reading_notes: Four roof details at 3"=1'-0": D1 roof edge, B1 roof edge/parapet, D3 vent thru roof, A1 gutter, A3 solatube prefab curb. 21 key work notes describing materials sequence: existing coated metal panel + 1 1/2" rigid insulation between flutes + 1/2" cover board + EPDM roof membrane. Pressure-treated wood blocking, prefinished metal coping, prefabricated pipe boot flashing, 12" solatube curb. Architect-sealed. Confirms the build-up assembly described narratively on A-001.

sheets.title: LIGHTNING PROTECTION ROOF PLAN — DEMOLITION
sheets.reading_notes: 1/8"=1'-0" lightning protection demo plan. Shows existing rooftop grid: perimeter conductor on grids A and E (top and bottom of building), 24 typical air terminals around perimeter, 4 corner air terminals, vertical down conductors at four corners. 5 demolition notes: disconnect/remove rooftop LP grid (salvage), remove air terminals (salvage), remove antenna and wiring (dispose), existing down conductor must remain, disconnect/remove circuit to exhaust fan back to panel source. Sealed by Richard H. Williams, PE (BFA, VA Lic. 048025). Designer: RHW; Drawn: RFD. Note 'Exothermic welds are prohibited' — JLab convention, likely radiation-area rule given accelerator-facility context.

sheets.title: LIGHTNING PROTECTION ROOF PLAN — NEW WORK
sheets.reading_notes: 1/8"=1'-0" lightning protection new-work plan, mirrors ED-101 layout. 3 construction notes: reinstall LP grid conductor and connect to existing down conductors and through-roof penetrations (damaged conductors replaced with No. A24 Class 1 copper, 24 strands of 14 AWG); reinstall air terminals (damaged replaced with 1/2" x 12" minimum solid copper equivalent); reconnect to existing down conductors. Note 3 specifies third-party UL-certified post-construction testing with master label certificate. BFA-sealed. Designer: RHW; Drawn: RFD. The conductor (A24/Class 1) and air terminal (1/2" x 12" solid copper) specs follow NFPA 780 / UL 96A typical practice.

conflict_flags.rationale: PO line-item description is a clerical transcription error. The bound task order document (which the PO references) explicitly says 'Project Title: 87 Re-Roof Design'; the project narrative on A-001 says 'Building 87'; all 7 drawings are titled 'BUILDING 87 RE-ROOF DESIGN'; PE/architect seals are dated and reference Building 87. Single isolated PO description error vs. consistent designation across all other source artifacts.

4 of 5 pages say Task Order No. 3; p. 4 (the submittals-quantity table page) says No. 2 — almost certainly a copy-paste artifact from a prior task order template. Task Order No. 3 is the consistent designation.

Seal dates are the most defensible 'design complete' date because they reflect what was actually delivered.

conflict_flags.rationale: The PO is issued directly to BFA, which is the strongest evidence of prime contract holding. But the actual architectural design content is sealed by Dills Architects, who appear in their own title-block panel labeled 'DA Dills Architects' alongside the JLab title block. Most likely interpretation: BFA is the prime A-E (holding the JSA contract) with Dills as BFA's architectural sub. The taxonomy.bfa_role would then be ['prime_consultant'], not subconsultant. Without an explicit teaming-agreement document or letter of agreement to confirm, the encoding is ambiguous. Flagged for human review and Pass-1 retro.
